clue.text: Quite dry in quarry

indicators.note: the word in tells us the dry piece sits inside the quarry piece

parts.note: quarry is the hunted animal, prey
TT, teetotal, means not drinking: dry

explanation.surface: A remark that a quarry is rather arid.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adverb, as in 'fairly good', the word is a synonym of quite.

clue.text: Fish speed northward forcefully

indicators.note: in a down clue, going northward means reading upwards, so backwards

parts.note: clip is speed, as in a fast clip
hard means with force

explanation.surface: A fish swims north at speed with great force.
explanation.definitionFit: The pilchard is a small oily sea fish of the herring family.

clue.text: Second person in garden, around noon, cut swathe

indicators.note: around says the first woman's name goes round the noon letter

parts.note: Eve was the second person in the Garden of Eden, after Adam
to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: Someone else in the garden at midday mows a broad strip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swathe' looks like a noun for a cut strip of grass, but it is the verb meaning wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: To swathe something is to wrap it up completely, to enclose it.

clue.text: Figure, taking catch, upset all Australia in finish

indicators.note: taking joins the catch word to what follows

parts.note: a trap is something that catches

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the whole combined piece upside down
in places the Australia letters inside the finish word

parts.note: to die is to finish, come to an end
Oz is a nickname for Australia

explanation.surface: A geometry figure, after a dropped catch, upset all the Australians at the end of the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset all' turns the whole container result upside down (DIOZE becomes EZOID), not just Australia's letters; in a down clue 'upset' reads bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapezoid is a geometric figure, a four-sided shape.

clue.text: Stop nark making compromise

parts.note: to stop something is to end it
to nark is to annoy or anger someone

explanation.surface: Halting an informer leads to a deal being struck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nark' looks like the British slang noun for a police informer, but here it is the verb meaning irritate. 'compromise' is the verb, as in putting someone's safety at risk.
explanation.definitionFit: To compromise someone's safety is to put it at risk, the verb's threatening sense.

clue.text: Tiny one in class gets in trouble for silliness

indicators.note: getting into trouble suggests things in disarray, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: The smallest child in the class is punished for being foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: All fourteen letters of 'Tiny one in class' are the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonsensicality is the quality of being absurd, foolishness.

clue.text: Storyteller when full of energy on top of work

indicators.note: in a down clue on top of means placed above, so first
full of says the first piece contains the energy letter

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
E is the symbol for energy
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A storyteller, full of energy, rises to the top of his work.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek teller of fables.

clue.text: Set clothes near rumpled blanket

indicators.note: clothes as a verb means dresses, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: to gel is to set, as jelly does

indicators.note: rumpled means creased and disordered, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A tidy set of clothes left beside a crumpled blanket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rumpled' turns NEAR into NERA, which GEL 'clothes'.
explanation.definitionFit: Blanket as an adjective means covering everything, all-inclusive, like a general rule.

clue.text: Next thing to do? Arrange holiday destination

definitions.meaning: read as ..., to sort again, put in order
a seaside or ski town where people go on holiday

explanation.surface: Planning what to do next and booking a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition: the hyphenated re-sort gives the 'Arrange' sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers a recourse, a sorting again, and a holiday town.

clue.text: Dreamlike film about Chinese navigator endlessly on journey on river

indicators.note: about means the film word goes round all the rest

parts.note: a pic is a film, short for picture
the Han are the majority ethnic group of China

indicators.note: endlessly takes off the final letter of the navigator's name

parts.note: Abel Tasman was a Dutch navigator who reached Tasmania and New Zealand
to go is to journey

explanation.surface: A surreal film about a Chinese explorer's endless voyage down a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The navigator is not Chinese: he is the Dutchman Abel Tasman, and 'Chinese' is a separate piece. Everything from HAN to R sits inside the film word.
explanation.definitionFit: Phantasmagoric describes a shifting, fantastic sequence of images, as in a dream.

clue.text: Knight follows through, cutting up all but tail of deadly monster

indicators.note: follows puts the knight's letter after everything else
cutting up says one piece slices into the middle of the other
everything except the final letter of the deadly word is kept

parts.note: deadly is a synonym of lethal
via means by way of, through
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A knight follows through with his sword, carving up a deadly monster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'through' looks like part of the knight's sword stroke, but it is the preposition via; 'all but tail of' leaves LETHA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Leviathan is the biblical sea monster, so the name stands for any huge monster.

clue.text: Hollow act regarded as wrong by our team

parts.note: a sin is an act regarded as morally wrong
us is the speaker's own side, our team

explanation.surface: A hollow gesture deemed foul play by our side.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinus is a hollow cavity, especially in the bones of the skull.

clue.text: Artist abandoned bile, overwhelmed by love

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means the scrambled letters are engulfed inside the love word

parts.note: hon, short for honey, is an endearment like love

indicators.note: abandoned in the sense of wild and unrestrained signals the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A painter gives up his bitterness, swamped by affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' makes LBEI. 'love' is not O here, as it so often is in crosswords, but the endearment hon.
explanation.definitionFit: Hans Holbein the Younger was a German painter at the court of Henry VIII.

clue.text: Monarch in tune with leader removed by soldiers

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter, which is taken off

parts.note: to temper an instrument is to tune it, as in the well-tempered clavier
OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A king who is harmonious, once his chief has been ousted by the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word. 'with leader removed' drops the T from TEMPER, leaving EMPER, which is placed 'by' OR.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor is a sovereign ruler of an empire, a kind of monarch.

clue.text: Resistance faced by salesman with old copy

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A salesman with an antique duplicate meets opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: A repro is a reproduction, a copy of an original such as furniture or a print.

clue.text: Group skilfully skirting hole, going round

indicators.note: skirting means going around the edge, so this piece encloses the other

parts.note: ably means with skill

indicators.note: going round turns the hole word to face the other way

parts.note: being in a hole is being in a mess, a predicament

explanation.surface: A golfer's party skilfully avoids the hole as the round goes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' makes SSEM. The golf picture of skirting a hole hides the sense of hole as a predicament.
explanation.definitionFit: An assembly is a gathering of people, a group met together.

clue.text: Responsibility, being married, troubles character

parts.note: ills are troubles or misfortunes
tone is the character or quality of something

explanation.surface: Marriage brings troubles and shapes one's character.
explanation.definitionFit: A millstone round one's neck is an idiom for a heavy burden or responsibility.

clue.text: Envisaged protecting shelter against untrustworthy type

indicators.note: protecting means wrapping round, so one piece holds the others

parts.note: seen means envisaged, pictured
lee is shelter from the wind
V, short for versus, means against

explanation.surface: Someone imagined guarding a refuge against a shifty character.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is an Irish and Newfoundland dialect word, rare enough that the wordplay is the surest route to it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Irish English a sleeveen is a sly, crafty, untrustworthy person.

clue.text: Plug in fantastic device to transmit sound of educational kind

indicators.note: in places the plug piece inside the fantastic piece

parts.note: ace means excellent, fantastic
a plug is a piece of publicity, an ad
a mic, short for microphone, picks up and transmits sound

explanation.surface: Instructions to plug a marvellous sound device into the school system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plug' looks like an electrical connector, but it is an advert.
explanation.definitionFit: Academic means relating to education and scholarship.

clue.text: Deception over sanction

parts.note: a con is a deception, a swindle
done means finished, over

explanation.surface: A trick that is finished earns approval.
explanation.definitionFit: To condone is to allow or approve of wrongdoing, to sanction it.

clue.text: Tag line first to get done to death

indicators.note: first places the line letter at the start

parts.note: Abel, in Genesis, was killed by his brother Cain

explanation.surface: A slogan, line first, that has been used to the point of tedium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'done to death' looks like the idiom for overused, but it means killed: Abel was the first murder victim in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A label is a tag attached to something to identify it.

clue.text: Facts of life? Offer a word of gratitude, taking nothing in

indicators.note: taking together with in means the offer word takes a letter inside it
in completes taking ... in, putting the nothing letter inside

parts.note: a bid is an offer, as at an auction
O looks like zero, nothing
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: Someone thanks another while refusing to accept anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Facts of life' suggests sex education, but here it is a personal record, a life story in facts.
explanation.definitionFit: Biodata are biographical details, the facts of a person's life such as on a CV.

clue.text: Bishop in east with mission

indicators.note: in places the bishop's letters inside the other pieces

parts.note: and means with, together with
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop in the East on a mission.
explanation.definitionFit: An errand is a short trip made to do a task, a mission.

clue.text: Published piece in position

parts.note: a paper ran a story when it published it
the king is a chess piece

explanation.surface: A printed item about someone's standing.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranking is a place or position in an ordered list.

clue.text: Secret revealed by one having success losing weight

indicators.note: losing means one letter is dropped

parts.note: a winner is someone who succeeds

explanation.surface: A dieter's secret success is revealed after losing weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner thoughts are private and hidden, so inner means secret.

clue.text: Graceful plant turning into whopper?

indicators.note: into says the turned plant goes inside the whopper word

parts.note: a whopper is a big lie

indicators.note: turning makes the plant word read backwards

parts.note: moss is a small flowerless plant

explanation.surface: Does an elegant plant grow into something enormous?
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses MOSS to SSOM, put 'into' LIE. 'whopper' suggests something big, but it is a lie.
explanation.definitionFit: Lissome means supple and slender, moving with grace.

clue.text: Improve appearance of service after fuss

indicators.note: after puts the service letters behind the fuss word

parts.note: ado is fuss or bother
RN, the Royal Navy, is the Senior Service among the British armed forces

explanation.surface: A church service is spruced up after a lot of bother.
explanation.definitionFit: To adorn something is to decorate it, making it look better.

clue.text: Late on air, broadcast explanation

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered and reset

explanation.surface: An excuse given for a programme going out late.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the reasoning or justification behind something.

clue.text: Film star having selection of food loaded

parts.note: a diet is the selection of food one eats
loaded is slang for wealthy, rich

explanation.surface: A screen star with a choice menu who is very wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Marlene Dietrich was a German-born Hollywood film star.

clue.text: Recover, almost majestic at the wicket

indicators.note: almost means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: regal means kingly, majestic
in cricket, a batsman at the wicket is in

explanation.surface: A batsman recovers his form, looking almost regal at the crease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims REGAL to REGA. In cricket the side batting, or a batsman at the wicket, is 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: To regain something is to get it back, to recover it.
